slides.title: Merging? Decide the [brand] before the logo.
slides.lede: A law firm merger creates decisions about naming, positioning, partner authority and client confidence. Settle them before the new identity is commissioned.

slides.title: Decide which [clients and markets] the combined firm will compete for.

cards.label: Vague starting point
cards.text: Simply describing itself as a full-service law firm.

cards.label: Useful starting point
cards.text: Positioned around complex business disputes and transactions, matching genuine capability.

slides.title: Choose the name on [evidence], not size or seniority.
slides.note: A smaller firm may have a stronger reputation in a specialist market. **Size alone should not determine which name survives.**

slides.title: Can [partner-led service] survive at the new size?
slides.text: If both firms promise partner-led service, decide whether that remains operationally feasible with larger teams. Clients judge a firm through actual interactions, not its new colour palette.

slides.title: Give every brand decision an [owner] before design starts.

items.title: Establish the evidence
items.text: Brand assets, client feedback, referral sources, reputation.

items.title: Identify the decisions
items.text: Record what is agreed, disputed or deal-dependent.

items.title: Assign authority
items.text: Every decision gets an owner, approval route, deadline.

items.title: Commission the strategy
items.text: Only once direction and decision rights are clear.

slides.title: Plan when and how [each audience] hears about the change.
slides.note: Decide **when the new name becomes public**, how existing relationships are reassured and how expanded capabilities are explained.

slides.title: Start with the evidence. Agree the direction.
slides.lede: Pre-merger brand strategy starts with governance, not design. Read the full guide via the link in our bio.
